q: Under a realistic per-detector confusion / miscalibration model on the four Bell-state detectors D1..D4 (i.e., off-diagonal elements in the POVM), does the Bell-basis VQE's advantage in shot budget survive, or does the coupled error on {<XX>,<YY>,<ZZ>} amplify the energy variance enough to erase it? The paper's Fig. 3 asserts partial error mitigation for certain Hamiltonians but does not test this systematically across Hamiltonians; our replication did not implement a detector-noise model.
basis: The main VQE-E result reproduced exactly under multinomial (ideal) Bell sampling. We never added a noisy-detector POVM, so the paper's error-mitigation claim (C6) remains untested in this replication. A concrete follow-up would be to add a stochastic 4x4 confusion matrix to sample_bell() and rerun the VQE at multiple confusion strengths.
next_steps: Extend the shot-sampling routine to sample from a POVM {E_i = sum_j P(j|i) |Bell_j><Bell_j|} with an epsilon-parameterized confusion matrix; sweep epsilon in [0, 0.15] for both Heisenberg and HeH+; compare VQE energy error vs eps between the Bell and Pauli measurement paths.

q: The paper's Appendix-A HeH+ coefficient table (Fig. A1) and its 'E_th = -2.863 MJ/mol' at R=0.9 A differ by a clean factor of exactly 2 when compared to the ground eigenvalue of H = sum_j w_j sigma_j built from those tabulated coefficients (we found E_exact = -5.7252 MJ/mol). Which is the intended normalization -- is the paper's table pre-divided by 2 (a one-body anti-commutator convention), or is E_th reported per electron pair, or is one of the two just a unit ambiguity between MJ/mol and Ha x N_A?
basis: Building H directly from Fig. A1 row R=0.9 A gives -5.7252 MJ/mol; the paper says E_th = -2.863 MJ/mol. Ratio = 1.9997 (within 0.02%). Our best VQE (-5.7259 MJ/mol using the paper's grouping) matches our exact reference to <0.001 MJ/mol, so the factor-of-2 lives in the paper's stated Hamiltonian scale, not our code. This is likely a Psi4-JW normalization convention footnote that was omitted; without it a downstream reader cannot rescale confidently.
next_steps: Reproduce the coefficient generation directly with Psi4 v1.x + OpenFermion at R=0.9 A, print the raw one-body h_pq and two-body h_pqrs tensors, then trace which of the JW conventions (BasisNormalization normal-ordering constant, doubly-counted 2e- integrals, or an eV<->MJ/mol scale) accounts for the exact factor-of-2. Contact corresponding author yong-su.kim@kist.re.kr with a one-line clarification request.

q: For H2/STO-3G the greedy general-commutativity grouping collapsed 15 Pauli strings into just 2 groups (all-Z-diagonal + all XXYY-parity). But this collapse is possible only because 4-qubit fermionic parity gives especially large commuting families; how does this basis-count scaling behave as we go to H2 in a bigger basis (6-31G, 4-orbital, 8-qubit) or LiH? Does the Bell/GC advantage stay >30% or shrink, and is greedy-GC still near-optimal or does one need the harder graph-coloring formulation?
basis: H2/STO-3G at 4 qubits was a 'lucky' Hamiltonian: only two commuting families sufficed. The paper's Heisenberg/HeH+ cases are only 2-qubit; scaling behaviour is not addressed. Our greedy algorithm may be far from optimal at 8+ qubits; the paper cites QWC as NP-hard [20] but does not benchmark GC scaling.
next_steps: Generate the 8-qubit H2/6-31G and 12-qubit LiH/STO-3G Hamiltonians via OpenFermion, run greedy QWC, greedy GC, and (as an upper bound) a small MILP or NetworkX max-clique-cover on the commutation graph. Plot #bases and total shot cost (allocating shots by weight variance a la Rubin/Babbush) vs system size for each strategy.

q: In the Heisenberg VQE-E run under loose COBYLA tol=0.01 we observed much larger cross-run variance (std ~0.78) than VQE-P (std ~0.02), even though each Bell measurement returned a lower-variance <H> estimate at fixed shots (correlated estimates of <XX>,<YY>,<ZZ> from one basis). Tightening tol to 0.001 restored VQE-E to VQE-P quality. Is the COBYLA-tolerance -> optimizer-early-stopping interaction with correlated shot noise a systematic warning for practitioners who read the paper's tol=0.01 as canonical, or is it specific to our ansatz choice?
basis: Directly observed in R2: same shot budget, same ansatz, only difference is optimizer tolerance. VQE-E was harmed more by loose tol than VQE-P. The paper reports tol=0.01 without discussing whether the Bell method is more sensitive to this hyperparameter -- a potentially subtle usability issue for downstream users.
next_steps: Sweep COBYLA tol in {1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4} for both VQE-P and VQE-E on Heisenberg, plot final-energy std vs tol; do the same with SPSA (Kandala et al.) which is designed for noisy estimators. If the effect persists we should push a note to any users of the paper's protocol.

q: The paper uses a 2-qubit ansatz with 6 waveplate angles (hardware-native) but reports 'total number of shots is fixed to be N=9000' without saying how many shots the classical optimizer used per iteration vs how many trajectories were used to compute the reported std bar. Our VQE-P and VQE-E converged with ~50-75 COBYLA function evaluations at 3000 (resp. 9000) shots per evaluation; if the paper's N=9000 is total across all iterations rather than per iteration, then their per-eval shots must be <<100 and the energy estimator would be shot-noise dominated. Which interpretation is intended?
basis: We tried to match the paper's shot protocol and had to make an interpretation choice. Both interpretations reproduce the qualitative result, but they imply very different practical shot budgets in an experiment. This ambiguity matters for any group trying to translate the photonic-VQE cost accounting to another platform.
next_steps: Read the paper's supplementary or reach out to the corresponding author for the exact per-iteration shot allocation; if N=9000 is per iteration, redo the comparison at N=100 per iteration to expose the shot-noise-limited regime; publish both curves as a supplement.
